$schema: declarative eligibility taxonomy — shadow mode, phase 1 step 2
description: CURRENT behavior of the native-eligibility classifier, transcribed from native-eligibility-ast.ts / closure-eligibility.ts / instanceof-rhs.ts. Reason-keyed rows (verdict eligible|ineligible) are shadow-verified against the golden snapshot; contextual rows (verdict contextual, when:[imperative]) describe surface constructs whose verdict depends on shape predicates a flat row cannot evaluate — the phase-2 (consumption-inversion) backlog. No production path imports this file.

rows.rationale: A bare `{ … }` block statement has no body-stmt form.

A block-bodied arrow is eligible only when every statement is in the closure accept set (let/const/return/expr/if) with no rejected construct (this/await/loop/…); otherwise one of the closure-* reasons. Verdict depends on the whole block.
A labeled `break` has no body-stmt form.
A `break` outside any loop context.
A value-position assignment (e.g. const y = (x = 5)) inside a block-bodied arrow.
An `await` inside a block-bodied arrow — v1 closures are synchronous.
A `break`/`continue` inside a block-bodied arrow.
A class declaration/expression inside a block-bodied arrow.
A destructuring declaration inside a block-bodied arrow.
A value-position ++/-- (e.g. arr.push(x++)) inside a block-bodied arrow.
A labeled statement inside a block-bodied arrow.
Any loop (for/for-of/for-in/while/do) inside a block-bodied arrow — v1 closures reject loops.
A nested arrow/function/function-declaration inside a block-bodied arrow.
A raw closure block that does not parse as a single function body block.
A spread element/assignment inside a block-bodied arrow.
A `switch` inside a block-bodied arrow.
A `this` usage (incl. a this-rooted assignment target) inside a block-bodied arrow.
A `throw` inside a block-bodied arrow.
A `try` inside a block-bodied arrow.
An uninitialised `let`/`const` inside a block-bodied arrow.
A destructuring/parenthesized assignment target inside a block-bodied arrow (fail-closed).
An assignment operator outside {=,+=,-=,*=,/=,%=} inside a block-bodied arrow.
A statement outside the closure accept set (let/const/return/expr/if) inside a block-bodied arrow.
A `var` declaration inside a block-bodied arrow.
A `with` statement inside a block-bodied arrow.
A `yield` inside a block-bodied arrow.
A comment that does not sit at a migratable statement boundary; the migrator would drop it, so the body is rejected.
A labeled `continue` has no body-stmt form.
A `continue` outside any loop context.
A `do…while` statement has no body-stmt form.
A whitespace-only body is trivially eligible (classifyHandlerBodyAst returns reason "empty").
A compound assignment operator outside the supported set (e.g. logical &&=/??=).
An assignment target that is not a valid KERN assignment target (e.g. optional-chained).
An assignment value that is not a valid KERN assignment value.
An expression statement that is not a valid KERN expression (e.g. comma expression).
A prefix ++/-- whose source text the migrator cannot byte-reproduce (postfix is accepted).

An expression statement is eligible as a plain call/valid expression, a supported (compound) assignment, or a postfix ++/--; otherwise one of the expr-stmt-* reasons. Verdict depends on the expression shape.
A `for await` key-only/value-only entry binding — unsupported.
A `for await` over Object.entries(...) — unsupported async-entry shape.
The for-of iterable expression is not a valid KERN expression.
A for-of binding type annotation that is not a valid KERN type annotation.
A for-of object-destructuring binding (only [k]/[k,v]/[,v] array patterns lift).
A type annotation on a for-of destructuring binding is unsupported.
An empty for-of block body has nothing to emit.
A for-of declarator carrying an initializer.

A `for…of` is eligible only as a const, single-declarator, non-empty braced loop over a valid iterable with a supported binding shape; otherwise one of the for-of-* reasons. Verdict depends on header + body shape.
A for-of with more than one declarator.
A non-block for-of body (`for (...) stmt;`); `each` always braces (strict mode).
A for-of whose binding is not `const`.
A for-of whose initializer is not a variable declaration list.
A sync key-only/value-only binding not over Object.entries(...) (only entries=true emits those modes).
A C-style `for` / `for-in` statement has no body-stmt form.
Host-interop surface (res/process/db/req?., import(), useEffect, fetch, new Pool/AbortController) — stays a foreign boundary.

The whole handler body is eligible only when it parses, is not a host-interop/template/comment boundary, and every top-level statement is eligible. The aggregate verdict is the conjunction of all per-statement verdicts.
The if-condition is not a valid KERN expression.
A non-block, non-else-if else-branch (`else stmt;`) would lose byte-equivalence (strict mode).
A non-block then-branch (`if (c) stmt;`) would lose byte-equivalence; the emitter always braces (strict mode).

An `if` is eligible only with a valid condition AND braced (or else-if) branches whose statements are all themselves eligible; otherwise if-bad-cond / if-non-block-then / if-non-block-else. Verdict depends on branch shape.
An `instanceof` is eligible when its RHS is an identifier outside the reject set or a qualified member name; otherwise one of the instanceof-rhs-* reasons. Verdict depends on the RHS shape.
An instanceof RHS that is not an identifier or qualified member name (call/literal/binary).
A built-in RHS with no verified cross-target host mapping (Object/Date/Map/Set/…).
A primitive-wrapper RHS (String/Number/Boolean) — the wrapper-parity trap; fail-closed.
Every top-level statement (and nested if/try branch) maps to a body-statement form the migrator can emit.
The returned expression is not a valid KERN expression.
A returned template literal carrying a TS-only escape that diverges cross-target.
A returned template literal containing a raw newline.
A `switch` statement has no body-stmt form.
A template-literal const/return is eligible when single-line with only cross-target-safe escapes; otherwise *-template-multiline / *-template-escapes. Verdict depends on the literal contents.
A {{ ident }} mustache placeholder in an unparseable body — a templating boundary, not a lift gap.
The thrown expression is not a valid KERN expression.
A destructuring catch binding (`catch ({ e })`) cannot map to the body-stmt catch name.

A `try` is eligible with catch and/or finally, an identifier-named catch binding, and eligible branch bodies; a destructuring catch is try-destruct-catch and a catch/finally-less try is a parse error. Verdict depends on clause shape.
The body fails to parse as TypeScript and matches no foreign/template boundary — not migratable.
Any other statement kind (import/export-default-less/enum/interface/labeled/debugger/…) surfaces its SyntaxKind name.
The initializer expression is not a valid KERN expression.
The declared type annotation is not a valid KERN type annotation (round-trip-unsafe).
A destructuring binding whose shape the migrator cannot emit (incl. uninitialised destructure).
A destructuring initializer that is not a valid KERN expression.
A computed property name ([k]) in a destructuring pattern is unsupported.
A default value (= 1) on a destructuring element is unsupported.
An empty destructuring pattern ({} / []) binds nothing.
A nested destructuring pattern is unsupported.
A rest element (...rest) in a destructuring pattern is unsupported.
A declaration list with more than one declarator cannot map to a single body-stmt.
A `var` declaration; only `const`/`let` lift.
A template-literal initializer carrying a TS-only escape (e.g. \u{NNNN}) that diverges cross-target.
A template-literal initializer containing a raw newline cannot sit in a KERN attribute value.

A `let`/`const` is eligible only when single-declarator, identifier- or simple-pattern-named, with a valid type and a valid (or template) initializer; otherwise one of the var-* reasons. Verdict depends on declarator shape.
The while-condition is not a valid KERN expression.
An empty while block body has nothing to emit.
A `while` is eligible only with a valid condition and a non-empty braced body; otherwise while-bad-cond / while-non-block / while-empty-body. Verdict depends on body shape.
A non-block while body (`while (c) stmt;`); the emitter always braces (strict mode).
